items.t: Adyen stock gains JINS rollout across 150 Japanese stores
sum: Adyen announced on Monday, November 2, 2026, that Japanese eyewear retailer JINS HOLDINGS selected its platform for omnichannel payments. The company said the rollout will cover 150 Japanese locations from November, following an initial launch at JINS's Kichijoji flagship store in late September, according to Adyen.

The project brings JINS's online and in-store transactions onto Adyen's single platform. The setup is intended to give the retailer a unified view of payment activity, support operational efficiency and improve customer journeys across sales channels.

Adyen's mobile payment solution with Tap to Pay on iPhone will allow JINS employees to complete consultations, product selection and payment on the sales floor. Customers can finish purchases after choosing frames and completing an eye examination without moving to a central register.

JINS operates approximately 500 stores in Japan and has an expanding international footprint, the company said. Adyen's global payment infrastructure is intended to help JINS enter markets where the required payment services are supported without separate local integrations.

Adyen stock traded at 897.50 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 18:05 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026. Investors will focus on whether additional enterprise deployments translate into sustained payment volume and revenue growth. The JINS announcement did not disclose a financial contribution or a change to Adyen's financial outlook.
European payment technology stocks remain sensitive to merchant spending, digital commerce trends and expansion investment; see Current Euro Stoxx 50 market coverage for the broader regional context.

items.t: AEX closes at 1,129.22 points as chip selloff weighs on Amsterdam
sum: The AEX ended Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 1,129.22 points, down 0.62% from Wednesday's close of 1,136.29. The decline came as technology and semiconductor stocks weakened sharply across Europe and on Wall Street. The closing level and daily performance were reported by Reuters via Investing.com.

Technology was the main source of pressure. ASML fell 6.55%, ASM International lost 6.99% and BE Semiconductor Industries dropped 7.30%, according to the closing market report. The weakness followed a broad selloff in semiconductor shares, as investors reassessed the pace and durability of artificial intelligence infrastructure spending. Concerns about the effect of the US midterm-election outcome on data-centre construction and AI investment added to the sector's pressure.

The move in Amsterdam also reflected a much weaker US technology market during the European close. The Nasdaq was reported to be deep in the red, while semiconductor stocks were hit particularly hard after recent earnings and outlook statements renewed questions about demand and valuation. The AEX's technology exposure made the Dutch benchmark more vulnerable to that shift in sentiment.

Several large constituents moved against the market trend. DSM-Firmenich rose 5.49% to 113.30 euros and was the strongest AEX performer. The company benefited after UBS raised its price target following its recent quarterly results. Adyen advanced 4.51% to 892.50 euros, while Prosus gained 2.77% to 38.02 euros.

Market breadth remained negative: 55 Amsterdam-listed stocks fell, compared with 36 gainers, while 13 were unchanged. The pattern indicates that the decline was broad rather than limited to a single index heavyweight, even though the semiconductor complex accounted for much of the AEX's headline weakness.

Thursday's session leaves the Dutch benchmark exposed to developments in global technology shares and to fresh evidence about the returns expected from AI-related capital expenditure. A rotation toward more traditional sectors offered some protection, but the performance gap between chipmakers and selected defensive or consumer-oriented companies remained pronounced. The next session will show whether the selloff stabilizes or continues to dominate European equity trading.

ElevenLabs Valuation Soars to $22 Billion as CEO Sets Sights on IPO Preparations by 2028
sum: Mati Staniszewski, CEO of AI voice technology developer ElevenLabs, said at a technology event in London that the company aims to complete preparations for an initial public offering (IPO) by 2028, though the final timing of a listing has not yet been decided.

The London-based startup pushed its valuation to $22 billion (approximately NT$720 billion) in September through a secondary sale of employee shares, exactly double the $11 billion valuation from its February funding round. The transaction was sized at $300 million (approximately NT$9.9 billion), mainly intended to let employees cash out early.

ElevenLabs first made its name with AI dubbing and voice cloning, but in recent years its operational focus has shifted to enterprise voice agents, helping customers automate processes such as customer service, appointments and insurance renewals. Enterprise customers now contribute 55% of revenue, and its voice agents handle more than 15 million conversations per week, triple the level in February.

On the financial front, the company disclosed in September that its annualized recurring revenue (ARR) was about $600 million (approximately NT$20 billion), implying a valuation of roughly 37 times ARR. That same month, ElevenLabs recruited Ethan Tandowsky, a finance veteran who helped take payments company Adyen public, as chief financial officer — a move widely seen as laying groundwork for a path to the capital markets.

On the product side, the company recently launched a tool that can identify synthetic speech within real-time audio streams, targeting organizations such as government agencies that may struggle to cope with a surge in AI-agent calls. European Union transparency rules also impose disclosure obligations on certain AI interactions and deepfake content.
On the competitive front, ElevenLabs faces challenges from Alibaba's Qwen models and U.S. startup Fish Audio.
It is worth noting that as the company signals its IPO preparations, EY has pointed to signs of a recovery in the UK IPO market in 2026.

Adyen stock wins JINS rollout across 150 Japanese stores
sum: Adyen stock traded at 830.20 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:30 CET on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The payments group is drawing investor attention after a new Japanese retail partnership and a strong third-quarter update that also brought a lower profit-margin outlook.

Adyen announced on November 2 that JINS HOLDINGS, the operator of Japan's JINS eyewear brand, had selected its platform for omnichannel payments. Following an initial launch at the Kichijoji flagship store in late September, JINS plans to roll out Adyen across 150 Japanese locations starting in November, according to Adyen's announcement.

The project combines online and in-store payment data on one platform. Store employees will be able to complete consultations, product selection and payment on the sales floor using Adyen's mobile solution with Tap to Pay on iPhone. For JINS, the architecture is intended to reduce checkout friction and simplify expansion into international markets where Adyen supports the required payment services.

Adyen's business update for the quarter ended September 30 showed net revenue of 738.1 million euros, up 23% from a year earlier or 22% at constant exchange rates. Processed volume rose 30% to 451.1 billion euros. Digital net revenue increased 16% to 387.4 million euros, while Unified Commerce revenue climbed 29% to 250.5 million euros and Platforms revenue advanced 46% to 100.2 million euros.

The official Q3 release said early enterprise wins and the integration of Talon.One and Orb were supporting the broader platform. Adyen also highlighted partnerships with GetYourGuide, LillyDirect, Tod's and Toast, as well as work with Sierra and Meta on a protocol for interactions between artificial-intelligence agents and businesses.

Management kept its 2026 constant-currency net-revenue growth target at 21% to 23%. It now expects an EBITDA margin of 50% for the year, compared with the previous expectation of about 52%, and discontinued its medium-term EBITDA objective. Reuters reported that the change reflects accelerated investment in teams, products and platform capacity rather than a deterioration in the current revenue trend.
The revised margin outlook is the central investment issue for shareholders.

Adyen beats Q3 revenue estimates but shares sink 10% on margin outlook cut
sum: Investing.com -- Adyen NV (AS:ADYEN) shares sank more than 10% Wednesday after the company's full-year margin outlook cut overshadowed a quarterly revenue beat.
The company reported third-quarter net revenues of €738 million, up 22% on a constant currency basis YoY, beating analyst consensus by 1%.
The payment processor's total payment volume grew 30% YoY to €451 billion, accelerating from 25% growth in the second quarter and exceeding analyst estimates of €436 billion.

The revenue growth was supported by contributions from recent acquisitions Talon.One and Orb, though the exact contribution was not disclosed. The company's take rate came in at 16 basis points, up 1% sequentially but 2% lower YoY.

However, Adyen lowered its 2026 EBITDA margin target to approximately 50% from 52%, citing accelerated investments in Talon.One and Orb teams. The company also withdrew its 2028 margin ambition of 55%. The revised EBITDA guidance sits approximately 3% below analyst consensus at the midpoint.

"While the EBITDA margin cut/waive will lead to some discussion today, we see it net positive given the commitment to topline growth and encouraging commentary on both acquired businesses," Jefferies analysts said in a note.

Adyen's Digital segment saw payment volume increase 28% YoY, with net revenue of €387 million, up 16% YoY. The company attributed growth to wallet share gains in Travel & Mobility and Content & Subscriptions verticals.

Adyen Plans Bigger Push into India, Backs Long-Term Growth
sum: Dutch payments company Adyen is expanding its business in India and hiring more staff. The company believes India's digital payments and cross-border trade market has strong long-term potential.

Adyen's Asia-Pacific president, Gary Yang, said the firm will keep growing its team in India. He did not share exact numbers for future hiring or revenue. But the trend so far is clear. Adyen's staff count in India has grown tenfold since 2023. The company had about 120 employees in the country in the first half of 2026.

India's payments market is known for strict rules. Other firms, including some major players, have had difficulties. Stripe exited India in 2024, resulting from regulatory challenges. In 2021, PayPal exited domestic payments and now focuses only on cross-border payments.

Adyen has opted for a different path. In 2024, it was given the license to operate as a payment aggregator in India for domestic and cross-border payments. The company also set up a tech hub in Bengaluru. This hub supports its operations and product work in the country.

Adyen's India numbers back its confidence. Pre-tax income from its India business more than doubled in 2025. It rose to EUR 3.18 million, up from EUR 1.45 million in 2024. Globally, Adyen posted a net income of EUR 1.06 billion in 2025.
Also Read: Top 10 FinTech Startups in India Reshaping Financial Services in 2026

Adyen works with global firms like Adobe on their India payment plans. It also helps Indian companies, such as travel platform Oyo, expand abroad. The company has adjusted its systems to fit India's rules. This includes data storage laws, recurring payment mandates, and support for UPI, the country's popular payment system.

Epos Now Turns Its POS Into Financial Operating System for Small Business
sum: The point-of-sale system sitting on a small business counter has quietly become one of the most consequential financial decisions that owner will make — not because of which card networks it accepts, but because of whether it will also lend them money, hold their deposits, and issue cards to their staff. Epos Now, the UK-headquartered cloud POS provider, has completed a five-year buildout that answers that question with a yes across all four product categories. Working with global payments platform Adyen's embedded finance platform, the company now offers merchants a single interface for payments processing, business banking, working capital, and corporate card issuing — a stack that, until recently, required four separate vendor relationships and four separate reconciliation workflows.

The timing matters. A new five-year agreement between Epos Now and Adyen, signed to mark the original partnership's milestone, extends the infrastructure bet through the early 2030s. The full embedded suite — Payments, Capital, Accounts, and Issuing — is now live in the UK with a US rollout underway; Epos Now Capital for working capital is already available across Australia, Canada, Spain, and the US.

Epos Now spent most of its history doing what most POS companies do: it sold software and hardware to small and mid-sized businesses and passed payment processing to third-party referral partners. That arrangement had a structural flaw the company has since been explicit about. By operating a referral model, Epos Now had no control over the merchant experience — cost, service quality, and the ability to build new financial products on top of the payment relationship were all out of reach.

The pivot began with payments. Once Epos Now owned the payment processing relationship, the rest of the stack became architecturally accessible. "Once payments are in place, adding accounts, cards, or capital becomes just another click," Jason Downing, Epos Now's SVP of Product Management, explained in a conversation hosted by Adyen's Carlos Hernandez at Epos Now's headquarters. That sequencing logic — payments as the foundation, then financial products surfaced contextually as a merchant's needs emerge — mirrors the playbook Toast, Square, and Shopify have used to transform their revenue structures.

PYPL Stock Surges To 6-Month High On $53B Takeover Bid – Wall Street's Divided On Whether It's A Good Deal
sum: - Wall Street analysts were divided on Stripe and Advent International’s offer of $60.50 per share to acquire PayPal.
- BTIG said the board would consider the offer “seriously,” while William Blair suggested the offer may undervalue the company.
- Jefferies said the transaction would likely have a limited competitive impact on Adyen because the combined company would remain focused on consumer payments.

PayPal (PYPL) shares surged to a near six-month high on Wednesday after Stripe and private equity firm Advent International reportedly offered $60.50 a share to buy the company. However, analysts are split on whether or not PayPal should take the offer.

PYPL’s stock jumped as much as 18% in midday trade on Wednesday, marking highs last seen in January. It was among the top trending tickers on Stocktwits at the time of writing. Retail sentiment around the shares improved to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ territory over the past day, while chatter climbed to ‘extremely high’ from ‘high’ levels.

In a note to investors cited by TheFly, BTIG kept a ‘Neutral’ rating on PayPal’s stock but told clients the board will likely take the offer seriously, given what it called a "significant state of uncertainty" hanging over the stock.

William Blair, which has a ‘Market Perform’ rating on the stock, said it's "hesitant to chase" the rally. It stated that new CEO Enrique Lores may not accept without pushing back, calling it a potential "low-ball offer."

items.t: Down 72% From Its Highs, Is Former Market Darling Adyen Stock Finally a Buy?
sum: Although the broader market has soared amid the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, many stocks that were huge winners during the COVID-19 pandemic are still faltering. There may be no better example than Adyen (OTC: ADYEY). The payments giant is down 72% from its 2021 high, severely underperforming the market.

Investors are concerned about some slowing growth and a recent executive departure. However, if you look at the company's financial performance, you'll see it has created significant long-term value. Does that make this former market darling a buy in 2026?

First, let's talk about the bad. In early 2026, Adyen revised its revenue growth outlook for the year to a range of 20% to 22%, which was below its initial projections and analyst expectations of closer to the mid-20s. The revision led to a sharp drop in the stock price.

Then, in May, Adyen's chief financial officer announced a surprise resignation. Although there was no reason to believe it was due to performance issues at the executive level, investors never like it when a key leader in a business unexpectedly departs. To pile on, Wall Street analysts downgraded Adyen stock in early June over concerns about pricing for enterprise clients in Europe.
Altogether, Adyen stock has fallen 42% year to date, with investors as pessimistic as perhaps they've ever been on this payments stock.

Adyen's goal is to have the best payment processing capabilities, both online and offline, for enterprise retail clients. That's the reason global restaurant chains and the likes of Uber and Spotify use its services to process what can amount to billions of payment transactions every year.

To expand the value it provides to these merchants, Adyen has made two acquisitions this year, of Talon One and Orb. Talon One uses software to give shoppers real-time incentives to drive more checkout volume, while Orb helps software enterprises optimize pricing and manage customer billing. Both can work in tandem to drive revenue growth for Adyen clients. Since Adyen earns a percentage of all payment volume processed through its systems, these acquisitions should accelerate revenue growth if they're properly integrated into the businesses.

Here's Why Wall Street And Big Tech Are Uniting Behind A Stablecoin To Rival Circle And Tether
sum: - Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, BlackRock, and Coinbase are backing Open USD, a new stablecoin aimed at challenging USDC and USDT.
- OUSD will share reserve income with partners, unlike incumbents such as Circle and Tether, which retain most of that revenue.
- The consortium also includes major banks, fintechs, crypto firms, and tech companies, while Circle, Tether, and PayPal are not participating.

On Tuesday, a coalition of major payment, banking, and crypto firms, including Visa (V), Mastercard (MA), Stripe, BlackRock (BLK), and Coinbase (COIN), is backing a new dollar-pegged stablecoin called Open USD (OUSD).

The stablecoin was being developed by Open Standard in an effort that would challenge market leaders Circle's USD Coin (USDC) and Tether's USDT. Partners for the new stablecoin include BNY, Standard Chartered, BBVA, and DBS.

Fintech firms including Adyen, SoFi (SOFI), Klarna and Shopify (SHOP), and crypto firms like Coinbase, Gemini, Galaxy (GLXY), Ripple (XRP), Crypto.com (CRO) and Polygon (POL), as well as tech giants like Google (GOOGL) and IBM (IBM), also participated as partners for the new stablecoin.

Together, Circle (CRCL) and Tether (USDT) control roughly 80% of the more than $300 billion stablecoin market. According to a Bloomberg report, Tether, Circle, and PayPal (PYPL) will not participate in the Open Standard project.
